subject: Reference request: Extending R-INLA for 3D regullar lattice data

messages.author: 45d4b5de643596b5
messages.subject: Reference request: Extending R-INLA for 3D regullar lattice data
parts:
Hi all,

For my master's thesis I am working to implement several spatial models for fMRI data in R-INLA. The data contains only a single time step, corresponding to a summary of all temporal slices. I am currently working with the subcortical regions, which can be considered as a three-dimensional regullar latice. Each participant's data is stored as vector of length 30.000 x 1 containing the BOLD signal / acitivation amplitudes.

Yesterday I created a TsparseMatrix-class adjacency matrix based on the voxel coordinates to push the adjacent neighbors to the inla()-function. This seems to be accepted by the function. Now I am trying to figure out how to send all the data of the 1000 participants to the inla-function.

Are there any references you are aware of on how to work with 3D data for multiple subjects? I found many resources on 2D problems, and on how the SPDE approach can be used together with mesh structures. However, as I have regular lattice data, the SPDE approach seems unfeasible / unnecesarily complex. I also found papers on Bayesian spatial modeling for fMRI data, but the accompanying code isn't very transparent, and is largely adopted for cortical surface fMRI.

Any help is greatly appreciated.

Best,

Bas

Dear prof. Rue,

Thank you responding to my question even at this hour over the weekend. The model should perform binary classifications of each voxel, categorizing them as either on or off. Either I want to explicitly model this, or use some kind of threshold to extract this from predicted activation amplitudes. I am using a task fMRI task, so the question is really what voxels are activated by the task and which aren't. Using multiple subjects would increase the power, I assumed. 

Dr. Bolin is actually a (co-)author of the models I want to implement and extent. Hopefully he'll have time to look at my e-amil. I appreciate the recommendation. 

Have a good Sunday,

Bas Matsuura
